title: Pop Culture Parade
description: A fun, accessible pop culture board for any crowd — classic catchphrases, beloved animated films, chart-topping pop stars, superhero showdowns, iconic boy bands and girl groups, and unforgettable movie quotes.

questions.question: On Fox's long-running animated sitcom, this rotund nuclear plant safety inspector expresses his frustration with a single grunt — 'D'oh!' — whenever things go inevitably wrong in the town of Springfield.
Steve Carell's bumbling Dunder Mifflin branch manager on NBC's 'The Office' punctuated almost every accidental double entendre with this inappropriate two-word punchline: 'That's what she said.'

On CBS's 'The Big Bang Theory,' this Caltech theoretical physicist — played by Jim Parsons — crowned every successful prank on his roommate Leonard with a single invented word that sounds vaguely German: 'Bazinga!'

Two metalhead best friends who host a cable-access show out of a basement in Aurora, Illinois — played by Mike Myers and Dana Carvey — close every episode with this mutual affirmation: 'Party on, Wayne! Party on, Garth!'
Neil Patrick Harris played this suit-obsessed womanizer on CBS's 'How I Met Your Mother,' who stretched a single adjective into a multi-syllable verbal event: 'Legen — wait for it — dary!'

In this beloved 1994 Disney film, a young lion cub named Simba is wrongly blamed for his father Mufasa's death by his scheming uncle Scar, and must journey home to reclaim his rightful place on Pride Rock.

In this 2003 Pixar adventure, an overprotective clownfish named Marlin crosses the entire ocean — with help from a lovably forgetful blue fish named Dory — to rescue his son from a dentist's aquarium in Sydney, Australia.

In this 2001 Pixar film, a large blue monster named Sulley and his wisecracking one-eyed green partner Mike work for an energy company powered by children's screams — until a fearless little girl named Boo unexpectedly follows them home.

In this 2004 Pixar blockbuster, a family of secret superheroes living in suburban anonymity must come out of hiding to stop a supervillain who was once rejected by the superhero father as a wannabe sidekick.

In this 2002 Disney film set in Hawaii, a little girl adopts a small blue creature she thinks is a dog — unaware he is actually Experiment 626, an alien designed for destruction — and teaches him that 'ohana means family.'

This New York-born pop superstar made headlines in 2010 by wearing a dress made entirely of raw meat to the MTV Video Music Awards, and first conquered the charts with her 2008 debut single 'Just Dance.'
This pop powerhouse from Boca Raton, Florida rose to fame on Nickelodeon's 'Victorious' before releasing massive chart-topping hits including 'Problem,' 'God Is a Woman,' and 'Thank U, Next.'

When her 2010 album 'Teenage Dream' produced five number-one singles on the Billboard Hot 100 — including 'Firework,' 'E.T.,' and 'California Gurls' — this pop star matched a record previously held only by Michael Jackson's 'Bad.'

At the 2012 Grammy Awards, this British soul singer won six trophies in a single night — including Album, Record, and Song of the Year for '21' and 'Rolling in the Deep' — in a triumphant comeback after vocal cord surgery.

At the 60th Grammy Awards in 2018, this Honolulu-born singer-songwriter made history by winning all six of the categories he was nominated for — including Album of the Year for '24K Magic' and Song of the Year for 'That's What I Like.'

Faster than a speeding bullet and able to leap tall buildings in a single bound, this DC Comics hero disguises himself as mild-mannered Daily Planet reporter Clark Kent — his only weakness being a glowing green mineral from his home planet Krypton.

Unlike most superheroes, this billionaire who protects Gotham City at night has no superpowers whatsoever — just extreme wealth, a utility belt packed with gadgets, and a deep-seated grudge against criminals.

In the 2008 Marvel film that launched the entire MCU, genius billionaire Tony Stark builds a high-tech suit of armor while held captive in a cave, and Robert Downey Jr.'s charismatic performance as this armored hero set the tone for superhero movies for years.

This Marvel superhero rules the fictional African nation of Wakanda — the world's only source of the super-metal vibranium. His 2018 solo film, starring Chadwick Boseman, was the first superhero movie ever nominated for the Academy Award for Best Picture.

Gal Gadot played this DC warrior princess from the island of Themyscira in a 2017 blockbuster set during World War I, where she wields a lasso of truth and indestructible bracers while battling Ares, the god of war.

In 1996, Victoria, Mel B, Emma, Mel C, and Geri burst onto the global pop scene with 'Wannabe,' each sporting a fun nickname — Posh, Scary, Baby, Sporty, and Ginger — while championing their now-iconic philosophy of 'girl power.'

Harry Styles, Niall Horan, Liam Payne, Louis Tomlinson, and Zayn Malik were put together by judges on the UK's 'The X Factor' in 2010 and went on to become one of the best-selling boy bands in history.

This Philadelphia R&B quartet dominated the slow jam charts in the early 1990s with heartbreaking ballads like 'End of the Road' and 'I'll Make Love to You,' winning over fans worldwide with their signature four-part harmonies.

Brothers Kevin, Joe, and Nick made their mark through Disney Channel in the mid-2000s, built a massive teen fanbase, went on hiatus in 2013, then reunited in 2019 with their comeback single 'Sucker' — which debuted at number one on the Billboard Hot 100.

Before Backstreet Boys or *NSYNC redefined the boy band phenomenon, this Boston-formed quintet — including Donnie Wahlberg, Joey McIntyre, and Jordan Knight — blazed the trail in the late 1980s and early 1990s with hits like 'Hangin' Tough.'
questions.answer: Who are New Kids on the Block?

questions.question: Throughout this beloved galaxy-spanning sci-fi franchise, Jedi masters, rebel generals, and brave pilots offer each other this hopeful farewell before heading into danger: 'May the Force be with you.'

Arnold Schwarzenegger's unstoppable cybernetic assassin calmly makes this three-word promise — before driving a car through a police station wall — in James Cameron's 1984 sci-fi thriller: 'I'll be back.'
In Rob Reiner's 1992 military courtroom drama, Jack Nicholson's bombastic Marine colonel snaps at Tom Cruise's navy lawyer with this now-legendary outburst: 'You can't handle the truth!'
questions.answer: What is A Few Good Men?

questions.question: Sitting on a park bench and sharing chocolates with strangers, Tom Hanks's lovable protagonist delivers his mother's famous wisdom in this 1994 Best Picture winner: 'Mama always said life was like a box of chocolates — you never know what you're gonna get.'

Heath Ledger's Joker — in full face paint and a purple suit — haunts heroes and villains alike with this chilling three-word whisper in Christopher Nolan's 2008 Batman sequel, for which Ledger posthumously won an Academy Award: 'Why so serious?'
